newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says refugees not forced back to Burma.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says refugees not forced back to Burma.

text.p: The Thai army has never forcibly repatriated Karen refugees to Burma, but instead has offered them safe shelter away from border fighting, a senior officer was reported as saying on Sunday.

Major General Thaweep Suwannasing, commanding general of the Royal Thai Army's ninth infantry division in charge of the Thai-Burma border, denied reports of forced repatriation in an interview with the Bangkok Post.

"The fact is, when Army Commander-in-Chief General Chetta Thanajaro knew the Burmese refugees were crossing the border, he ordered the division to provide them with temporary shelter in a safe area away from the border until the situation returns to normal," Thaweep said.

Burmese troops sacked mobile bases of the Karen National Union (KNU) guerrilla organisation in the eastern part of the country last month in attacks that sent thousands of refugees and guerrillas scurrying for shelter into Thailand.
About 70,000 Karen refugees have been housed in sprawling camps in Thailand since the 1980s.
Thaweep said the Thai government did disarm fighters and request them to return to Burma voluntarily, but it allowed the fighters' family members or supporters into the country unarmed.
The United States and human rights organisations lashed out at Thailand last month for allegedly forcing the refugees back into Burma .
Washington accused the Thai army of forcibly repatriating Karen males, including boys as young as 10 years old, and of denying asylum to several hundred others.
Thaweep accused the KNU of committing human rights abuses.
"Talking about human rights violations: who really violated the rights of the young boys when the KNU recruited 13-year-olds and above into the fighting force?" he asked.
Burma has said it is willing to take back any Karen refugees wanting to return home.

The KNU, formed in 1948 to win greater autonomy for Karen State, has rejected several peace overtures from Burma's military government and remains one of the few ethnic guerrilla groups still fighting Rangoon.
